new_interfaces.example: For the existing illustrative pin /pɪn/ example, [pʰɪn] is a possible context-sensitive phonetic description. It is not a measured token. The spelling, broad form and phonetic description must remain separate.
new_interfaces.label: Phonology Phonetics interface
new_interfaces.limitation: A variety, stress and segmental context must be stated. This bridge does not assert a universal phonetics–phonology boundary or an executable production model. No audio has been recorded or inspected during migration.
new_interfaces.statement: Phonological representations constrain possible phonetic analyses without uniquely specifying an observed speech token.

new_interfaces.example: The existing Nina repaired the PRINTER illustration uses capitals to mark a proposed prominence pattern. Capitals contain no measured fundamental frequency, duration or intensity values.
new_interfaces.label: Prosody Phonetics interface
new_interfaces.limitation: The relation is schematic and potentially many-to-many, but its cardinality remains unspecified here. Acoustic cues, speakers and contexts need empirical investigation; an abstract prominence label does not predict numerical measurements.
new_interfaces.statement: A prosodic prominence analysis must be distinguished from the phonetic measurements used to investigate its realization.

new_interfaces.example: The questions Who repaired the printer? and What did Nina repair? provide different constructed contexts for Nina repaired the printer. They do not make a permanently fixed topic or focus an intrinsic property of the sentence string.
new_interfaces.label: Discourse Information Structure interface
new_interfaces.limitation: This is a QUD-compatible working bridge, not a consensus theory of discourse. Context may be insufficient to identify one topic or focus; alternative analyses must remain explicit.
new_interfaces.statement: A stated discourse context constrains an information-structure analysis without making grammatical Subject, Topic and Focus interchangeable.

new_interfaces.example: This report is ready and These reports are ready are constructed contrasts for relating nominal number and verb form in a restricted descriptive analysis. Their orthographic differences alone are not a universal agreement algorithm.
new_interfaces.label: Morphology Syntax interface
new_interfaces.limitation: Agreement varies by construction and variety; syncretism can conceal feature differences. This is a proposed bridge based on existing distinctions, with external claim support pending.
new_interfaces.statement: Word-form features and syntactic distributions must be represented separately even when an analysis connects them through agreement or finiteness.

new_interfaces.example: The existing RUN locomotion and management distinctions illustrate why run a company cannot be interpreted by selecting a spelling and ignoring lexical sense and construction.
new_interfaces.label: Lexicon Semantics interface
new_interfaces.limitation: The location of lexical and constructional information differs among theories. This bridge is schematic and does not establish an exhaustive sense inventory, an automatic disambiguator or full claim-level support.
new_interfaces.statement: A sense-specific lexical entry constrains an interpretation without making a spelling identify one context-independent predicate.
